diagnosis.explanation: Baseline P113 shows extremely low UV transmission (G1 ~2.1e-6) due to high absorption in Nb2O5 layers (k~0.8 at 267nm). Local derivatives indicate that decreasing specific high-index layer thicknesses (e.g., layer_4, layer_6) could reduce total absorption (helping G1) but may compromise stopband depth (hurting G2/G3). Refining individual layer thicknesses within the existing family bounds allows testing if asymmetric thinning of absorbing layers can recover UV signal without collapsing the visible/NIR rejection.

Design P036 (F006) uses a non-quarter-wave Nb2O5/MgF2 stack. It achieves moderate UV transmission (G1 ~0.008) but poor visible rejection (G2 ~0.43). Derivatives for variables t1, t3, t5 suggest that increasing these high-index layer thicknesses hurts G1 (absorption) but helps G2 (reflection). A refine_layers action is chosen to decouple these shared variables, allowing independent adjustment of specific high-index layers to find a local optimum that balances the trade-off between UV passband loss and visible stopband gain.

P007 (F001) is a symmetric Fabry-Perot design with a thick cavity. Compared to P006, it has lower UV transmission but better visible rejection in the blue subband. The family parameterization links mirror layers (dH, dL). A refine_family action is selected to simultaneously adjust the shared mirror thicknesses and cavity length. This explores the hypothesis that scaling the entire mirror period while tuning the cavity can shift the passband peak closer to 267nm and widen the stopband, addressing the spectral mismatch observed in the subband means.
